idiom_name: module-scope Map (or module namespace) registry plus dynamic import() for late binding
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no platform container and mostly does not need one: a module exporting a Map (or an object of factories) with register/resolve is the registry, and because a module is evaluated once per realm, its bindings already behave like a process-wide singleton - the module namespace replaces the ServiceLocator class. Late binding uses dynamic import(), which loads and evaluates a module on demand and resolves with its namespace object, so a name from configuration can select an implementation without a build-time dependency. Build the registry at the composition root (the entry module) and export a lookup function; a container library such as awilix (container.resolve) or tsyringe is an opt-in alternative worth its weight only when you need decorator-driven constructor injection or scoped lifetimes.
pitfalls: Module scope is per module instance, not per process: a duplicated package (two node_modules trees, a bundled plus an unbundled copy) yields two registries and "unregistered service" at run time.
Circular imports can hand a module an empty registry, because the importing module runs before the exporter finished; register from the entry point rather than from module bodies.

Tokens must be identity-stable (a Symbol, the class itself, a frozen token object): two structurally equal objects are two different keys, so plain strings or ad-hoc objects drift as soon as a rename happens.
